hooks.text: A 190-meter asteroid snuck past Earth closer than the Moon.
Did a skyscraper-sized asteroid just miss us without warning?
We missed a massive asteroid until it already passed us.

title: The Asteroid We Didn't See Coming
description: In 2018, a massive asteroid passed closer to Earth than the Moon, but solar glare kept it hidden from telescopes for days.

beats.text: A 190-meter asteroid snuck past Earth closer than the Moon.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a 190-meter asteroid compared to the Washington Monument

beats.text: It zipped by at 297,000 kilometers in 2018.
beats.visual: diagram showing the distance between Earth, the Moon, and asteroid 2018 AH

beats.text: But astronomers didn't even know the rock was there.
beats.visual: photograph of the ATLAS telescope facility at night on Mauna Loa, Hawaii

beats.text: This giant asteroid approached from the direction of the Sun.
beats.visual: artist's concept of an asteroid silhouette against the bright Sun

beats.text: Solar glare kept the massive rock invisible until it passed.
beats.visual: photograph of the Sun showing intense photosphere glare and corona

beats.text: Experts finally spotted it two days after its closest approach.
beats.visual: photograph of an astronomer looking at data screens in the ATLAS observatory

beats.text: It matches the 1908 blast that leveled entire forests.
beats.visual: historical photograph of thousands of flattened trees from the Tunguska event

beats.text: An impact would have unleashed a 12-megaton explosion.
beats.visual: photograph of a massive mushroom cloud from a nuclear test explosion

beats.text: We only saw the danger once it safely moved away.
beats.visual: artist's concept of asteroid 2018 AH receding into the darkness of deep space

better_than_last: Corrected the emphasis in beat four to ensure literal string matching and followed the one-number-per-beat hypothesis for improved cognitive processing.
